div.head: ECf retr 39.1
div.ab:
Uociferabantur etiam ciues et burgenses et populus pro suis consuetudinibus, eo quod circa festum sancti† Mar
tini consueuerant animalia in foro mercari sine plegio ad suas occisiones contra natale† Domini faciendas.
div.note: Liebermann’s text transcribed from Gesetze I p. 669–670 (November 2026): read from the page images and checked against the scan’s own text layer, differences settled against the page; the words in bold are the Retractator’s changes to ECf, as Liebermann prints them.
Liebermann prints daggers after “sancti” and after “natale”, and gives in the outer margin the dates †Nov. 11 and †Dec. 25.
Liebermann’s numbering of the notes in the ECf retr column starts again at 1 on p. 670.

div.ab: The citizens and burgesses and the people also clamoured on behalf of their customs, because around the feast of St Martin† they had been accustomed to purchase animals in the market without a pledge to make their slaughterings against the Nativity† of the Lord.
